statement: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 500 ms, a size-aware normalized multiplicative-gate rank-power ruin score (scale removal_savings by per-instance mean savings and by n, gate on route load fill / depot distance, and raise the rank exponent p monotonically with stagnation_ratio while annealing it down with iter_frac) reduces mean objective below the round-1 SBS of 16.0353, with the largest gains on the weak regimes size=100, spatial=uniform, depot_style=eccentric, demand_dist=uniform, capacity_level=loose.
rationale: Rounds 1-4 all used the same skeleton (16.0353 -> 16.1564 monotone drift worse), so remaining headroom is in the destruction priority hook. KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 reports that the multiplicative-gate rank-power form beats worst-cost removal (23.3186 vs 23.3474 on blind_120) and that its advantage comes from stagnation-aware diversification. On dev_24 the weakest regimes are n=100 and uniform-spatial, where a fixed-rank top-q ruin over-focuses on a few high-savings nodes; normalizing savings and growing the rank exponent with stagnation should spread ruin over more routes, while the load-fill gate keeps removals from emptying near-full routes and wasting capacity slack (loose-capacity regime).

rationale: Round 5 evaluated the size-aware normalized rank-power ruin hook on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 (24/24 valid, all feasible, completion 1.0, solve_ms_mean=348.59). Mean tour length = 15.844548 vs round-1 SBS 16.035307 (delta -0.190759, ~-1.19% relative) and vs the round-4 solver 16.156409 (-0.311861). This is the largest single-round objective improvement in the session and confirms that evolving the score_ruin_nodes destruction priority (mean-depot-distance normalization of removal_savings + rank-percentile transform + load-fill gating + stagnation-driven rank power) is a real source of headroom on top of the shared CW + intra_2opt + Regret-2 + R2R skeleton, consistent with the blind_120 finding in method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 that the multiplicative-gate rank-power ruin beats worst-cost removal. Caveat: the regime-level claim (largest gains concentrated on size=100 / uniform / eccentric / loose) cannot be individually confirmed from the aggregate dev result alone, so only the mean-level claim is marked supported.

rationale: Re-opened as testing. The mean-level claim of H5 remains the round-5 incumbent (15.8445, -1.19% vs round-1 SBS 16.0353), but the round-6 regime-adaptive extension of the same hook scored 15.898268 (24/24 valid, all feasible, completion 1.0), i.e. +0.339% worse than the H5 incumbent and therefore a regression. Key secondary observation: solve_ms_mean dropped 348.59 -> 221.81 ms at identical coverage, so the round-6 edit (asymmetric edge-fill gate + extension-coupled depot gate + bounded p schedule + early top-q shrink for large n) purchased cheaper iterations rather than better ones. H5's regime clause (largest gains on size=100, spatial=uniform, depot_style=eccentric, demand_dist=uniform, capacity_level=loose) is still unattributed — round-6 returned regime_summary=null and the archive's weakest-regime list has since moved to capacity_level=tight, contradicting H5's stated loose-capacity emphasis. Consequence for next round: keep the round-5 kernel as incumbent, restore or raise the ruin-set size q to consume the ~278 ms of idle budget, and change one factor at a time (gate shape vs q vs p schedule) so the regime attribution can be resolved.
